summary.headline: Adani Power Q2 FY27 continuing EBITDA rose 18.5% to INR6,321 crore on 11.5% higher volume; reported PAT jumped 141.5% to INR7,019 crore, aided by INR2,422 crore one-time prior-period revenue.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 volumes grew 11.5% to 26.4 BU at 70.1% PLF, with PPA realisation up 12.7% and short-term merchant tariffs up 33% per unit. Continuing revenue rose 29.8% to INR17,014 crore, while fuel cost rose 41.8% to INR10,229 crore on a roughly 50% higher landed cost of imported coal. Reported PAT was lifted by a one-time INR2,422 crore prior-period revenue from Gujarat PPA rate revision, partly offset by a INR19.7 billion (about INR2,000 crore) reversal of Haryana DISCOM alternate coal claim revenue. Management reported a credit rating upgrade to AA+ and a 1,320 MW Uttarakhand 25-year PPA award, and said the first 660 MW Korba Phase-II unit has synchronised to the grid.

segments.name: PPA (long and medium-term)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 29.7% to 23.4 BU on higher DISCOM offtake and a larger operating PPA base; PPA realisation up 12.7% on a continuing basis, supported by import coal pass-through and new medium-term PPAs.

segments.name: Merchant and short-term
segments.commentary: Volumes down 43% YoY as open capacity was moved into medium-term contracts; short-term merchant tariffs rose 33% per unit.

segments.name: Hydro (GVK Alaknanda, 330 MW)
segments.commentary: Entered hydro generation after being declared successful resolution applicant for GVK Energy under CIRP; no Q2 contribution was quantified on the call.

guidance_outlook: Normal expected thermal PLF is about 65%; Q2 (70%) and H1 (74%) were above norm due to weak hydro, and management expects a return to 65%.
Korba Phase-II Unit 1 (660 MW): grid synchronised, commercial commissioning expected shortly / Q3 FY27 per Nishit Dave; Unit 2 (660 MW) expected around December 2026 / Q4 FY27.
Mahan Phase-II (1,600 MW) commercial operations targeted for early FY28.
Peak debt expected around INR1 lakh crore by FY30 or FY31, nearly double current levels, per CFO.
Finance costs expected to remain largely flat despite higher market interest rates, supported by the AA+ upgrade.
Gujarat indexed fuel pass-through from the Q2 imported coal rise is expected to show up in tariffs only from about Q3 FY27 due to the indexation lag.
Capacity to reach about 45 GW by 2032 (42 GW organic plus 3 GW inorganic), per management clarification; management said it may revisit its capacity-addition strategy.
capex_capacity: Portfolio about 18 GW operating; 24 GW thermal pipeline with PPAs signed for 62% of it.
Uttarakhand Power Corporation 25-year PPA for 1,320 MW (fixed charge INR4.30) from upcoming Korba-2; PPA begins after about 4 years, so the capacity will be sold medium-term or merchant until then.
Raipur Phase-III: 1,600 MW ultra-supercritical plant to take the Raipur site to 4,570 MW and supply a second long-term PPA to a Maharashtra DISCOM.

Bhutan: shareholders' agreement with Druk Green Power for a 770 MW hydro project (49:51 JV), second Bhutan project after 570 MW Wangchhu; MoU for 5,000 MW total, with 1,340 MW now covered by shareholder agreements.
Bid pipeline: UP bid submitted with opening expected this month or early next month; West Bengal 1,600 MW bid due early next month; Rajasthan bid due first week of next month.
Nuclear: draft rules out for comments, comment process complete; notification expected soon before the capacity expansion proceeds.
demand_pricing: India power demand rose 11.5% YoY to 502 BU in Q2; peak demand reached 270 GW; thermal PLF nationally 68% vs 62%.
Management says power exchange tariffs rose substantially and short-term merchant tariffs were up 33% per unit.
Domestic coal: Coal India notified prices unchanged, but effective cost rose slightly on lower-quality monsoon coal.
Imported coal landed cost up about 50%; Gujarat indexed tariffs pass this through with a lag of more than 6 months.
Bangladesh PPA is linked to international prices, so benefits flow through immediately.
Haryana DISCOM: about INR2,000 crore (50% of claim received) of alternate domestic coal compensation revenue derecognised for conservative accounting pending settlement.

qa_highlights.question: Did the lag in tariff versus imported-coal fuel cost hurt Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gujarat indexed tariffs cover fuel costs, but margins were slightly lower because the rise has not yet passed through; it is expected to reflect from Q3 after the indexation lag. Bangladesh PPA reprices immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Haryana DISCOM alternate coal claim revenue reversed despite receiving money?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 50% of the claim (about INR19.7 billion) was received, but issues from 2021-23 are unresolved, so on auditor advice the amount was reversed until settlement. Management does not foresee a net interest outgo, but cannot rule out a small provision.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR5,000 crore annualised EBITDA increase without new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Nishit Dave cited full-year utilisation of capacity acquired in FY26, medium-term PPAs replacing intermittent merchant sales, tariffs linked to international coal, and Tuticorin (Mutiara) running on 35-40% domestic coal with PPAs for both 600 MW units.

qa_highlights.question: Are finance costs sustainable given higher gross debt?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said net debt was flat at about INR45,000 crore, GUVNL receipts of about INR6,000 crore helped, and finance costs are expected to stay largely flat despite higher market rates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2032 capacity target 42 GW or 46 GW?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the target is about 45 GW, comprising 42 GW of new capacity plus 3 GW from pending inorganic acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Will Lanco/Korba capacity be sold, and when does it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Korba is assigned to the Uttarakhand PPA, which starts after about 4 years; until then it will be sold medium-term or merchant, with coal from linkage or auction depending on the route.

risks_watch: Fuel-cost pass-through lag: Gujarat indexation means the Q2 imported coal spike reaches tariffs only from Q3, so Q3 margin depends on coal prices.
Haryana DISCOM alternate coal claim: about INR2,000 crore reversed, with settlement and possible interest provision still open.
Quality of one-time revenue: INR2,422 crore prior-period income inflated Q2 reported PAT; Q3 run-rate needs to be watched.
Debt build-up: gross debt INR61,860 crore, with peak expected near INR1 lakh crore by FY30/31; finance cost flat assumption depends on rates.
Commissioning timelines: Korba-2 Unit 1 and Unit 2 (around Dec 2026), Mahan Phase-II early FY28; Korba-2 PPA start about 4 years away.
Bid outcomes: UP, West Bengal (location-specific) and Rajasthan (state-specific) bids; Gujarat and UP bids allow sites anywhere in India.
Management declined to provide segment-level EBITDA split (merchant vs energy charge) on the call, offering a follow-up with IR.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pricing and expansion, calling the quarter a record. More guarded on the Haryana claim reversal, nuclear timing, EBITDA targets and granular guidance, where management deferred to one-to-one follow-ups.
